Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork into dated dossiers, each containing a document index, account identifiers, field-level metadata, and channel-of-receipt notations, maintained in closed status after settlement with no further intake processing.

2) What occurred: The actor created multiple duplicate digital ticket documents referencing a single valid ticket record for a sold-out event. Each duplicate document was formatted with the same event fields, seat identifiers, and cryptographic hash fields as the source document. The actor transmitted the duplicate documents to a buyer via a messaging channel. The actor coordinated timing so the buyer's document scan occurred at a gate terminal before the source document. The actor used the original account's refund field access to block refund processing and monitoring of chargeback flags on the payment account.

3) Materials/access observed: One valid digital ticket document with event date field, seat number field, and hash verification field. Multiple duplicate ticket documents with altered serial fields. A named buyer account. A messaging channel for document transfer. A payment account with refund and chargeback fields. Gate terminal scan logs with timestamp fields. An account holder profile record.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Duplicate ticket documents sharing identical hash fields with differing serial fields. Multiple scan events on the same seat field at the same event. Transfer of ticket documents across accounts via a non-institutional messaging channel. Suppression of refund processing on a settled account. Chargeback flag manipulation on a payment record. Mismatch between account holder profile and document presenter identification fields.
